subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Does any current authenticated client, plugin, or Gateway RPC path accept nested or recursively composed predicates that reach the SQLite-backed audit or task ledger?
rationale: The named files and documented APIs do not show the alleged path, but only a security owner can safely confirm the complete exposed query surface and decide whether authenticated-operator resource exhaustion warrants additional controls.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Audit all ledger query entry points and close this issue if every exposed schema is closed, bounded, authorized, and unable to construct recursive predicates.

options.title: Scope a concrete hardening fix
options.body: If a richer ingress exists, document its caller role and payload, then add typed complexity and request-budget enforcement at that ingress with a current-main denial-of-service regression test.

options.title: Adopt general operator throttling
options.body: Add broader authenticated query throttling only as an intentional control-plane availability policy after evaluating legitimate automation and support-query workloads.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Audit all ledger query entry points and close this issue if every exposed schema is closed, bounded, authorized, and unable to construct recursive predicates.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP observability and runtime history plus the explicit issue mention make this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-boundary audit.
